verdict.rationale: Make's own webhook docs say incoming requests can be held in a queue and processed on a schedule instead of running immediately. That is a first-party way to defer and batch executions, which can ease pressure on downstream systems. However, nothing documents explicit throttling, concurrency caps or rate-limit-aware execution control. Missing for 10: explicit execution throttling or rate-limit settings, concurrency limits, queue controls beyond webhook scheduling, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can throttle or queue workflow executions to respect downstream rate limits

citations.quote: If you don't want to run your immediately after a webhook receives data, you can schedule your to process all webhook requests periodically
the whole queue is then processed every time your schedule criteria are met
